tasks.short: Schedule programming and read programming logs.

steps.what: Read television programming logs and authorized recording or airing requirements in the broadcast scheduling system {OTHER}
Schedule programming and check exact event IDs, durations, channels and recording destinations using native timing and collision checks in {OTHER}
Commit the checked programming schedule in {OTHER}

tasks.design: Configure native timing, asset-duration and channel-collision checks in the broadcast scheduling system {OTHER}. The technician still reads programme requirements and checks the final schedule before committing; actual on-air transmission is a separate operational action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Timing and channel conflicts can require repeated manual reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native schedule validation can calculate durations and flag overlaps.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting late programme changes and choosing priorities.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which authorized programme should actually run.

ambition.what: No extra output or automatic editorial scheduling is assumed.

tasks.altitude: Less timing arithmetic, unchanged programme accountability.

evidence.claim: Broadcast scheduling systems can validate timing and resource overlaps while technicians interpret requirements and authorize schedules.

assumptions: Boundary includes log reading and schedule preparation and commit, not playout operation or transmission. A log-reading-only occurrence has no schedule-entry saving.

Programme control supplies event ID, approved revision, start, duration and channel; media ingest supplies asset ID and actual duration. Technician confirms these in s1 and s2. Missing or stale values require manual reconciliation within retained work.

Native checks first; no model chooses content. Proposed shares are provisional work estimates. Ordinary commit retains full effort. Normal author check in s2 binds the final version and all destinations; edits void it.
unknowns: Share of occurrences requiring schedule entry rather than only log reading.
research_questions: Are timing checks already configured, and how much manual reconciliation remains?

already_counted.description: Reading actual programming requirements remains counted.

incremental.description: Maintain duration and channel validation settings.

approvals.approved_version: Exact schedule and destinations checked in s2; changes require recheck.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: In a scheduling occurrence, 35% less s2 effort saves 20.65 points less 1.5 upkeep. Low is read-only work or checks already configured.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct trainees in production equipment and media editing.

steps.what: Demonstrate television production equipment, event filming and copying or editing graphics and sound on the actual equipment
Observe trainees trying the procedures, explain errors and coach safe operation

tasks.design: Keep live equipment demonstration and corrective coaching with the technician. Existing operating instructions and editing software {OTHER} support instruction; generative media editing does not replace observing a trainee learning the equipment.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on seeing attempts and explaining the actual mistake.
tasks.enabler_now: No new tool removes this live instruction within the stated task.
tasks.still_hard: Adapting feedback to a trainee's understanding.

ambition.what: No new training programme is assumed.

evidence.claim: Editing aids automate media manipulation, but hands-on equipment instruction and observing trainees remain separate human work.

assumptions: Boundary is actual instruction, including demonstrations and trainee feedback. No attendance register, course design or report is named or assumed as a hidden part of the in-person steps; if required, allocate its actual effort separately before estimating benefit.
Training uses existing safe equipment, media and instructions supplied by training coordination. No structured trainee assessment is fabricated from scheduled attendance.

Native equipment help is already available; it is not a new saving. The digest's rough-cut and tagging capabilities concern production output, not the time to teach equipment use. No change means zero upkeep.
unknowns: Whether this workplace separately requires an instructor assessment record.
research_questions: Does any actual repeated training paperwork exist before proposing a form?

already_counted.description: Live demonstrations and observation of trainee attempts remain fully counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No live instruction is removed; production-editing tools do not establish a saving on this teaching task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Develop budgets by establishing broadcast scope, production assumptions and required equipment or staffing
Assemble cost lines and calculate budget totals and alternatives in {SPREADSHEET} using authorized rates and explicit quantities
Assess cost realism, contingencies and trade-offs and write the final proposed budget with checked assumptions
Save the checked budget proposal in {PROJECT}

tasks.design: Configure reusable rate lookups and explicit cost formulas in {SPREADSHEET}, using approved cost exports from {ERP}. The technician still sets quantities, assesses production risk and writes the final proposed budget before saving it in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated rate transfer and cost arithmetic obscure technical assumptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native lookups and formulas can calculate the same explicit cost lines.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing realistic production quantities and contingencies.
tasks.human_edge: Technical judgement about what the production will actually need.

ambition.what: No new financial authority is granted.

tasks.altitude: Spend more attention on production trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Spreadsheet lookups and formulas can assemble explicit cost lines while production assumptions and contingencies remain human choices.

assumptions: Boundary is developing and saving a proposal, not obtaining spending approval or placing orders. No approval-to-spend or external send is hidden in the save.

Finance supplies cost code, rate, currency, effective date and actual prior costs in an authorized export; the technician supplies quantity, duration and contingency in s1-s3. Missing rates require manual cost research within retained s2 effort.
Native formulas first; existing system runtime is excluded. All quantities and narrative justification remain human. Normal author check in s3 binds the exact proposed budget, not spending authority.
unknowns: Current formula coverage and availability of approved rates.
research_questions: Can rate lookups reduce repeated transfer without hiding expired quotes?

already_counted.description: Scope, resource assumptions and final trade-off assessment remain counted.

incremental.description: Update rate mappings and check formula changes.

approvals.approved_version: Final proposed budget checked in s3; edits require recheck.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Half of the 45-share rate-and-calculation step saves 22.5 points less 1.5 upkeep. Low is existing formula coverage or unsuitable rate data.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Discuss the client's production requirements, clarify deliverables and explain technical constraints
Record the actual production requirements and unresolved points in the existing project brief {PROJECT}, checking meaning and project identity

tasks.design: Use the existing project brief in {PROJECT} with project identity prefilled. The technician conducts the discussion and records the actual requirements; no transcript or inferred client agreement replaces this work.
tasks.previous_blocker: The small brief update may repeat project headers.
tasks.enabler_now: Native project-linked fields can reuse identity.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding ambiguous client aims and explaining technical limits.

ambition.what: No new client service is assumed.

tasks.altitude: Conversation and commitment authority remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Separate agreed needs from unresolved questions.

evidence.claim: Project-linked forms can reuse identifying fields but cannot determine what a client actually meant.

assumptions: Boundary includes the actual discussion and its existing brief update. No new confirmation email or contract acceptance is assumed. Internal talk uses read authority, not act_external.

The coordinator supplies project ID and client identity; the technician supplies actual requirement, constraint and unresolved point in s2. Missing identity is manually checked. All substantive capture remains.

Native fields first; benefit is only 10% of the small writing step, not the discussion. Ordinary save remains. The normal author check in s2 binds the exact update without an added self-approval step.
unknowns: Whether project identity is already prefilled.
research_questions: Is any header repetition actually present in the existing brief?

approvals.approved_version: Exact production-brief update checked in s2; edits require recheck.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Header reuse saves 0.9 points less 0.2 upkeep; no conversational saving. Low is identity already prefilled or no written brief for the occurrence.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use explicit native checks for schedules and costs while keeping live production decisions human.
reach: Support production coordinators with clear technical constraints.
role.ambitious_version: A technician who can explain schedule and budget trade-offs without automated editorial decisions.
